name: South Dakota
$scopeNote: South Dakota has NO state individual income tax of any kind, and never has -- it is one of the states whose constitution (Art. XI, sec. 2, via the sales-tax-in-lieu-of-income-tax structure adopted last century) has never been amended to permit one, not a phase-out state like New Hampshire. No local income tax anywhere: municipalities may levy local SALES tax (general municipal sales tax + a municipal gross receipts tax on lodging/alcohol/entertainment/restaurant meals) but South Dakota law does not authorize any city or county to levy a tax on wages or earned income. No employee-paid unemployment, disability, or paid-leave program of any kind -- Reemployment Assistance (South Dakota's name for UI) is funded entirely by the employer, and South Dakota has no state Paid Family/Medical Leave program at all (voluntary or mandatory) -- a genuine structural difference from Vermont/New Hampshire, which at least have a voluntary program on the books.

sources.title: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation -- Reemployment Assistance Tax FAQ
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly (raw HTML, not just the summarized fetch). Quoted verbatim: 'For calendar year 2026 and each year thereafter, an administrative fee of eight-hundredths percent (.08%) or .0008 must be paid by the employer. For calendar year 2025 and 2024, if the employer's reserve ratio is less than two and one-quarter percent, an administrative fee of two hundredths percent (.02%) or .0002 shall be paid.' This resolved a real apparent conflict on first read: the page ALSO shows a 0.55% 'Administrative Fee' column in the NEW-EMPLOYER rate table. These are two DIFFERENT fees, not a contradiction -- the 0.55% is a component of the flat new-employer rate (years 1-3 only); the 0.08% (up from 0.02%, effective calendar year 2026) is a SEPARATE fee under SDCL 61-5-24 that applies only to employers who have graduated to experience rating, i.e. NOT new employers. Confirmed by the page's own structure: the 0.08% clause appears directly under its own 'Administrative Fee' subheading, distinct from and below the new-employer rate table.

sources.title: South Dakota DLR -- Reemployment Assistance for Businesses (rate notices)
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched directly. Confirms the $15,000 taxable wage base (unchanged since 2015) and that '2026 rate notices were mailed to employers on Oct. 31, 2025' -- i.e. individual experienced-employer rates for 2026 are already final and notice-driven per employer, not something this engine can derive from a public table alone.

sources.title: Wilmington-style local-tax and UI cross-check (secondary, corroborating only)
sources.verifiedBy: Cross-source confirmation only, not independently fetched in full: corroborates no state or local income tax anywhere in South Dakota and the $15,000 UI wage base.

unemploymentInsurance.$comment: Employer-only (SUTA/RA tax) -- no employee contribution, confirmed directly. South Dakota calls this 'Reemployment Assistance' (RA), not 'UI', but it is the same FUTA-certified employer payroll tax as every other state's SUTA.
unemploymentInsurance.administeredBy: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation (DLR), Reemployment Assistance Tax Unit

newEmployerRates.comment: Investment fee 'applies to those with a positive account balance' per the source's own footnote -- a hold-harmless clause also caps an employer's investment-fee rate at their 1987 fee rate if their account had a positive balance at the end of the last two years, an unusual legacy provision unique to South Dakota's statute among every state built in this project so far.

2024and2025.condition: only if the employer's reserve ratio is less than 2.25%

experienceRatedAdministrativeFee.comment: A REAL rate change effective exactly this tax year: the administrative fee for experience-rated (3+ year) employers rose from 0.02% (and only for low-reserve-ratio employers) to a flat 0.08% for ALL experience-rated employers starting calendar year 2026 -- both a rate increase and a base-broadening in the same change. This fee sits on top of the reserve-ratio-based Schedule A/B contribution rate below; it is not a component of the new-employer table above.

experienceRatedSchedule.$comment: Reserve-ratio-based Schedule A/B contribution rate table (SDCL 61-5), 'Beginning 2018' vintage, transcribed from the FAQ page's own table -- comprehensive but not directly usable by this engine, same class of gap as Wisconsin's 26-row Schedule D table: applying it requires an employer's account reserve ratio, which nothing in types.ts carries.
experienceRatedSchedule.note: NOT a full transcription -- only a representative sample of the reserve-ratio bands was captured (the source table has many more rows spanning both positive and negative reserve ratios, plus a separate 2011-vintage Investment Fee table keyed by its own reserve-ratio bands). Flagged honestly as partial rather than padded out with unread rows; South Dakota has no state income tax, so this table is lower-priority than an income-tax bracket table would be, and was intentionally not pursued to full completeness in this pass.

unemploymentInsurance.knownGap: Experience-rated schedule is only partially transcribed (see note above), and even fully transcribed would need a reserve-ratio input this engine's types.ts doesn't carry -- same structural gap as every other state's experience-rated SUTA in this project.

localIncomeTax.rule: NONE. South Dakota has no constitutional or statutory mechanism for any city, county, or municipality to levy a tax on wages or earned income. Municipalities may levy local SALES tax (general + gross receipts on lodging/alcohol/restaurants/entertainment) -- a genuinely different tax, flagged explicitly so it isn't mistaken for a local income tax the way Wisconsin's county sales-tax table was flagged in that file.
localIncomeTax.confidence: cross_source_confirmed -- consistent across every source checked, no dissent found, but not tied to one specific enabling/prohibiting statute citation the way this project's strongest 'no local tax' claims (e.g. Wisconsin's) are.

paidLeave.rule: NONE. South Dakota has no state Paid Family/Medical Leave program, mandatory or voluntary -- a genuine structural difference from New Hampshire and Vermont, which each have at least a voluntary program on the books. Nothing to disclose as a knownGap here because there is no program of any kind to model, not an unmodelled one.

reciprocity.note: Not applicable rather than 'checked, none found' -- South Dakota has no income tax to be reciprocal about. reciprocalStates left structurally empty for consistency with every other state file's shape, same convention as New Hampshire's.

knownGaps: The experience-rated Schedule A/B contribution-rate table is only partially transcribed (4 of many rows) -- not pursued to full completeness because South Dakota has no income tax and the table is unusable without a reserve-ratio input this engine doesn't carry regardless of completeness.

Local-tax and UI figures rest on the DLR's own primary pages (strong) plus one secondary cross-check (onpay.com, not independently fetched in full) -- not a weakness specific to this file, but recorded per this project's standing confidence-tier convention.

suiEmployer.$comment: Normalized employer-side unemployment parameters — the shape src/taxes/state.ts reads. The detailed unemploymentInsurance block above stays the record of research; this exists because that block's shape varies too much between states to compute from directly (wage bases as objects, industry-keyed rate maps, differently-named keys).
